parts:
[back on the dev list; Evan, if you're not on the list,
you should join so you can reply -- this post involves you.]

You should be OK committing it now to the main
branch as long as it doesn't break the way things
currently run.

I'm not sure what you mean by debugging. I'd like
to sit down and go over what you did for error handling
and matrix operations.

We don't have unit tests for our commands -- they're
a little hard to test that way. If you created smaller
pieces of code, these should have unit tests. Daniel or
I can help you with the google test unit-testing framework.

I'm hoping Daniel will be able to add tests of the
full mass matrix version of NUTS to our other model tests.

For turning this into a paper (what you need to do to
get a good job post graduation), what you need to do is
some comparisons with diagonal-adaptation NUTS.
What we're looking for is (a) fast convergence, and (b)
high effective samples per second after convergence.

We can talk more about what specifically to do in the
next meeting. Evan B. was going to work on some of the
tests for NUTS vs. JAGS. It's probably best for students
if we produce a series of student-first-authored papers.

- Bob
